amenities.label: Aman-Curated Wellness Spa
amenities.sub: Treatment rooms, infrared saunas, cold plunge

amenitiesDescription: Amenity programming is organized around four pillars: movement, recovery, nourishment, and connection. Lower amenity floors are planned around an Aman-curated wellness spa with treatment rooms, infrared saunas, cold plunge pools, and a movement studio, with a rooftop saltwater pool and lounge spaces above. A dedicated lifestyle and wellness director is planned to lead longevity-focused programming. At the waterfront edge, a publicly accessible Baywalk of roughly 350 feet ties residents toward the Design District, Wynwood, and downtown.
description: Lilli Residences Edgewater is a rare Miami preconstruction bayfront proposition at 717 NE 27th Street: a fifty-three-story tower by OKO Group with one hundred seventeen private residences from $1.65 million. Adrian Smith + Gordon Gill Architecture shapes a sinuous glass silhouette above Biscayne Bay — terraces, light, and horizon composed for buyers who value restraint and scale. Request a discreet introduction to floor plans, finishes, and the early release program for this limited collection. Qualified interest is sequenced privately ahead of the next broader market release.
editorialLine: Curvilinear glass on the Edgewater bayfront, with 117 residences turned toward the water.

investmentThesis: Lilli is the second phase of OKO Group's multi-phase Biscayne Bay master plan, following the delivered Missoni Baia next door. OKO Group (led by Vladislav Doronin) pairs with Adrian Smith + Gordon Gill Architecture, whose Miami portfolio includes the delivered Una Residences on South Brickell. The collaboration signals architectural-first positioning on one of the last undeveloped bayfront lots in Edgewater. The developer publishes the tower at 636 feet across 53 floors with 117 residences, from one-bedrooms of 1,348 square feet to a 6,849-square-foot penthouse; pricing has been announced from about $1.65 million with delivery timing still to be confirmed. Early-cycle buyers are underwriting scarcity of bay frontage, a boutique unit count relative to height, and the same developer–architect DNA that produced a top-of-market South Brickell delivery.

residenceContent:
Lilli is planned as a 53-story bayfront tower along Biscayne Bay at 717 NE 27th Street in Edgewater: a sinuous glass silhouette with softly rounded balconies and floor-to-ceiling glass oriented toward the bay, Miami Beach, and the downtown skyline. The curvilinear form reads as movement in the skyline: continuous terraces, deep slab edges for shade, and a vertical rhythm that changes with coastal light from dawn through dusk.

Residences are expected to span one-bedroom layouts through expansive penthouses approaching 7,000 square feet, with ceiling heights reaching roughly twelve feet, layered stone and millwork, and chef-caliber appliance suites suited to serious entertaining. Interiors are conceived as calm counterweights to the drama of the glass: tactile materials, disciplined daylight, and private outdoor rooms that behave as extensions of the living space rather than shallow Juliet rails.

Parking is planned on a separate parcel at 527 NE 26th Street rather than in a tower podium, which keeps the bayfront massing slender. At grade, a tall glazed lobby faces the water, and landscaped edges connect residents to the public Baywalk. Delivery timing and final finish packages remain subject to developer release; the narrative here reflects the publicly disclosed design intent for the site.
